description:
The opt-in recorded-by-name tier of the lookup used to key a recorded decision on the source's literal spelling of its compartment, so a caller writing `Raw / in air` could not reach a decision BAFU recorded under `resources / in air` about the same place -- the tier answered only a caller who happened to spell a compartment exactly as some merged list had. #357: the key is now the name and the resolved consensus context, read from the build's own record of each outcome row's resolution.

Most of what a name-level count calls a collision dissolves under that key: `Carbon dioxide` reaches eight flows by name and one per place, and `Oxygen` as a resource from air is one decision three lists agree about. On the build of 30 August 2026 (20260830T1046047189150000), 15,756 distinct name-and-place keys hold exactly one recorded flow and 43 hold two. The 43 are genuine disagreements and decline rather than being arbitrated; see the sibling file for #359, which is about them.

expectations.title: Thousands of recorded name-and-place keys hold exactly one flow
expectations.comment: 15,756 on the 30 August 2026 build. Before #357 these decisions existed but were keyed on each source's spelling, so a caller's own compartment reached almost none of them.

expectations.title: The keys two lists disagree about are a fraction of a percent of the index
expectations.comment: 43 of 15,799 keys on the 30 August 2026 build -- 0.3%. The bound is loose on purpose: a new merged list adds vocabulary and may add disagreements, and that is information rather than a defect; what the claim rules out is the collision count of a name-only key, where `carbon dioxide` alone contributed seven.
